question: Does GraphicsEngine::Initialize (0x90e60) touch the disk in its six repeated rounds, and what are its helpers?
answer: No. Every helper in the six rounds is a pure in-memory operation.

helpers_resolved.0x1972c0: container insert: compares the requested slot against the container end and moves elements; no I/O
helpers_resolved.0x23090: operator new[]: divides to detect size overflow, checks the 0x1000 threshold and the 16-byte alignment, then allocates; no I/O
helpers_resolved.0x22ce0: std::string::assign on the small-string layout; no I/O

so_the_six_rounds_are: six constructions of BaseResourceManager-derived managers, each given a name string and the ResourceLoader, followed by container insertion. This is resource-manager bookkeeping, not resource loading.
additional_symbol: 0x19a830 resolves to ResourceLoader::StartThreads(), which confirms that the int passed to ResourceLoader(int) is a thread count.
significance: Because the six rounds perform no disk access, a host does not have to provide game data for GraphicsEngine::Initialize to complete. Combined with CreateDevice running before it, the whole device plus resource-manager setup is reachable without asset files.
not_established: whether the later engine subsystems in Engine::Initialize read data files
whether CreateDevice itself needs shader files present
the meaning of the four strings and five booleans
